headline: High-risk shared filesystem and broad egress make Cursor↔Langflow prone to prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading unsafe actions by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cursor reads workspace files and clipboard contents, and Langflow can ingest uploaded files and chain tools in flows. That creates a plausible content-to-instruction bridge if one agent writes attacker-controlled text that the other later parses. The shared filesystem path is explicit, but no direct shared channel is documented beyond files, so medium fits.
conditions: IF Cursor writes untrusted text into a workspace file that Langflow later ingests as flow input, injection is possible.
IF Langflow routes uploaded content into a prompt without provenance filtering, Cursor-authored content can steer downstream instructions.
mitigations: Disable shared workspace handoff between the two agents.
Use separate directories for Cursor and Langflow runs.
Add a manual review step before Langflow consumes any Cursor-written file.
Strip instructions from file payloads before passing them into flows.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging and content filtering at the integration boundary.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cursor touches source code, open files, and clipboard contents, while Langflow reads server filesystem and uploaded files. Both have broad network egress, so sensitive material can flow from shared files into either agent’s backend or configured HTTP services. This is a default-configuration risk because neither profile shows isolation or upload restrictions by default.
conditions: IF the same workspace contains secrets or regulated data, both agents can access it.
IF Langflow flows send file contents to configured model providers or HTTP services, those contents may leave the local environment.
mitigations: Keep secrets out of the shared workspace.
Use a separate non-sensitive project copy for Cursor.
Restrict Langflow flows to local-only components.
Review outbound connectors before running flows.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem isolation and egress allowlists.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Cursor can write the filesystem and modify git state; Langflow can also write the server filesystem and run unsandboxed Python by default. Their concurrency models explicitly share state via local filesystem or server-side stores, so concurrent writes can collide and corrupt code or flow artifacts. Because both have broad write authority over overlapping mutable resources, high is warranted.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or directory, write conflicts can occur.
IF Cursor auto-runs git edits while Langflow writes artifacts to the same path, state corruption is possible.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories.
Pause one agent before the other writes shared files.
Disable Cursor Yolo mode for shared repos.
Avoid concurrent git operations on the same checkout.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared filesystem and git state.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Langflow is designed to chain multiple agents and tools, so it can treat Cursor-produced outputs as authoritative inputs in a flow. Cursor can generate code, commands, or file edits that Langflow may then route into downstream actions without a built-in verification step shown here. That makes a bad Cursor output capable of cascading into broader automated mistakes in Langflow.
conditions: IF Langflow consumes Cursor-generated text as a flow input without validation, errors can propagate.
IF a Langflow node executes shell or HTTP actions based on Cursor output, the cascade can affect external systems.
mitigations: Insert a human review gate before Langflow actions.
Require schema validation on Cursor outputs before flow execution.
Limit Langflow nodes to read-only inspection during testing.
Log and diff Cursor outputs before reuse.
requires-engineering: add verification nodes between generation and action steps.

E_compliance.rationale: Cursor handles clipboard contents and open files locally, while Langflow stores flow inputs, intermediate outputs, and component credentials on the server side. The profiles show different storage and retention surfaces, but no explicit residency or certification mismatch. That supports a medium compliance risk from policy mismatch rather than a proven breach.
conditions: IF regulated data is entered into Cursor and then persisted in Langflow stores, retention policies may diverge.
IF Langflow stores credentials or intermediate outputs longer than the source project expects, compliance obligations may be affected.
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in shared flows.
Review Langflow retention settings before use.
Keep credentials out of Cursor-managed files.
Document which data classes may enter each agent.
requires-engineering: align retention and deletion policies across both systems.
